children: is set to post first quarter results on Thursday, after markets close.
Wall Street expects the networking gear maker to post EPS of $1.33 on revenue of $18.13B, implying a rise of 21.8% during the quarter.

Cisco, which is a supplier to cloud, enterprise, and communication services providers, has benefitted from higher demand for AI infrastructure from hyperscalers. The company booked orders worth over $9B from hyperscalers so far this year and said it sees over $7B in artificial intelligence-related revenue from the hyperscalers in 2027.
Over the last two years, San Jose, California-based Cisco

params.linkText: has beaten both revenue and EPS estimates

children: “Cisco has a strong history of beating top- and bottom-line expectations, and so I believe another quarter of outperformance is coming,” stated Seeking Alpha analyst Bay Area Ideas, adding that impacts from elevated memory costs, shifting revenue mix in favor of hardware, and intensifying competition in networking could remain in play for the first quarter.

Seeking Alpha and Wall Street analysts are bullish and rated the stock a Buy. In contrast, Seeking Alpha’s Quant ratings consider it a Hold. Over the last three months, EPS and revenue estimates have seen 19 and 17
, respectively, compared to no downward moves.

“We continue to see a multi-year trajectory for [double digit] growth, largely through cloud growth, helping CSCO sustain a higher multiple than historical,” said Morgan Stanley analyst Meta Marshall.
“However, cautious of degree of pullforward ahead of pricing increases and margin profile of cloud business, causing us to step to the sidelines for now,” added Marshall and downgraded the stock.
The stock has gained 30% so far this year, compared to the nearly 10% rise in the broader S&P 500 Index.

title: Cisco Q1 earnings on deck: What to expect
